goal.opening.intro.health:
Let's set your training goals and direction.
The direction is the big picture: what kind of body and what kind of training you want. A goal is a number along that direction: what, how much, and by when.
We'll fill in the card below together as we talk.
goal.opening.question.health: Is there a physique or a training goal you are aiming for?
goal.opening.examples.health:
e.g.
• a bodybuilder's physique
• finish a 10km race
• train 4 times a week
goal.move.activity_lead: Your last 4 weeks of workout records average {per_week} sessions a week.
goal.move.activity_lead_cal: Your calendar has '{title}' on {when}, and your last 4 weeks of records average {per_week} sessions a week.
goal.move.ask_activity.health:
I set your goal pace and training amount around what you do now.
How are you training these days?

e.g.
• the gym, about 3 times a week
• bodyweight at home now and then
• taking a break right now
goal.move.ask_training:
Your training history changes the goal and the program, so I need it.
How long have you been training like this?
goal.move.confirm_activity:
I set your goal pace and training amount around what you do now.
I have your training as {act}. Is that still right?
goal.move.confirm_activity_tr:
I set your goal pace and training amount around what you do now.
I have your training as {act}, for {tr}. Is that still right?
goal.move.ask_baseline.inbody:
The target numbers are set from where your body is now.
If you have your latest InBody sheet, could you send a photo of it?
goal.move.ask_baseline.weight:
I work out your daily calorie range from your weight.
How much do you weigh, in kg?
goal.move.pace_cadence: We measure with {cadence}; the weekday gets pinned to a training day once your training times are set.
goal.move.lift_state: {label} goes in as adding a little weight or a rep every session instead of a target number.
goal.move.lift_state_deficit: {label} goes in as adding a little weight or a rep every session instead of a target number; while eating less, not dropping counts as success.
goal.move.lift_stretch: I'll note {value}{unit} as your {label} target. Adding a little every session stays as it is.
goal.move.pace_now_fat: Body fat is about {kg}kg now (around {pct}% body fat). Let's set how fast to lose it by {horizon}, {weeks} weeks out.
goal.move.pace_d_kcal.down: {lo}~{hi}{unit} in {weeks} weeks, eating about {kcal}kcal less a day
goal.move.pace_d_kcal.up: {lo}~{hi}{unit} in {weeks} weeks, eating about {kcal}kcal more a day
goal.move.pace_p_base.down: Fast enough to see, slow enough to keep muscle and strength
goal.move.pace_m_fast.down: A bigger cut makes keeping muscle and strength tight
goal.move.pace_m_fast.up: Body fat may rise with it, or recovery gets tight
goal.move.pace_m_user_cap: About {kcal}kcal a day, above the {cap}kcal safety cap
goal.move.pace_rec.fat_up: Your muscle is rising, so I suggest option 1: lose fat while keeping it.
goal.move.pace_rec.fat: I suggest option 1: lose fat while keeping muscle.
goal.move.pace_capped: Options cutting more than {cap}kcal a day were left out.
goal.move.pace_floor: To keep the muscle, I left out any option that loses more than {kg}kg a week (0.7% of body weight) or has you eating under your {bmr}kcal BMR.
goal.move.pace_floor_rate: To keep the muscle, I left out any option that loses more than {kg}kg a week (0.7% of body weight).
goal.move.pace_floor_nobmr: There's no BMR on record yet, so I couldn't check that intake stays above it.
goal.move.held_lead_up: In the {weeks} weeks while {first} goes first you eat less, so raising {mlabel} is hard.
goal.move.held_m_user: Hard to reach in {weeks} weeks while eating less
goal.move.held_d_flip: Start with the phase that eats more
goal.move.held_rec_up: It comes much faster once you build volume than while cutting, so I suggest option 1.
goal.move.companion: For muscle we'll also watch the steadier {items}.
goal.move.ask_safety:
I set your goal so it does not strain anywhere you need to be careful.
Is there anywhere that hurts or that you need to be careful with?
goal.move.ask_safety_records:
I set your goal so it does not strain anywhere you need to be careful.
Your records list {sites} to be careful with. Is that still the same?
goal.move.ask_sex:
Muscle gain differs about two-fold by sex, so I use it to set your goal pace.
What is your sex?
goal.move.exp_from_records: your training records go back to {since}
goal.move.exp_from_pack: you said you're just starting to train
goal.move.exp_unknown: Training age is unknown, so I used the slowest rate
goal.move.share_records: converted with the muscle share of your {as_of} body-composition reading
goal.move.share_default: converted with a typical adult muscle share
goal.move.rate_fat: body fat drops about 1%p a month while keeping muscle
goal.move.rate_weight: {pct}% of your current weight per week (range {lo}-{hi}%) is a sustainable pace, so {kg}kg a week
goal.move.rate_muscle: for a {sex} with {exp} of training and {smm}kg of skeletal muscle, about {mo}kg a month is the natural pace
goal.move.noise_floor: {mlabel} wobbles about ±{sd}{unit} between readings (your {n} readings wobble less than the device study value, so the study value is used as the floor)
goal.move.noise_device: {mlabel} wobbles about ±{sd}{unit} per reading (few readings on record yet, so this is the body-composition-device research value)
goal.move.reading_off.up: The {date} InBody {mlabel} of {value}{unit} came out higher than the recent trend.
goal.move.reading_off.down: The {date} InBody {mlabel} of {value}{unit} came out lower than the recent trend.
goal.move.reading_water.up: The {date} InBody picked up more water, so {mlabel} may have read high along with it.
goal.move.reading_water.down: The {date} InBody picked up less water, so {mlabel} may have read low along with it.
goal.move.prac_lead: {axis} has no number to measure, so it goes into every session.
goal.move.prac_d.unilateral: One single-side move per session (e.g. lunge, one-arm row)
goal.move.prac_p.unilateral: Left-right gaps shrink and the body works as one
goal.move.prac_d.core: One loaded core move per session (e.g. hanging knee raise, cable crunch)
goal.move.prac_d.breath_trunk: One slow, controlled move per session that works breath and trunk together (e.g. roll-down)
goal.move.prac_p.core: The trunk holds steadier under heavy lifts
goal.move.prac_d.conditioning: A 6-8 minute interval at the end of the session
goal.move.prac_m.conditioning: Recovery can get tight while eating less
goal.move.prac_core_always: Core activation (dead bug, Pallof press and the like) goes into every session's mat prep whichever you pick.
goal.move.prac_rec_onesided: Only one side bothers you ({sites}), so option 1, training each side on its own, helps function and the injury at once. I suggest option 1.
goal.move.prac_rec_conditioning: You mentioned conditioning, so I suggest option 3.
goal.move.prac_rec_default: Single-side moves show and close left-right gaps, so I suggest option 1.
goal.move.card_lift: add a little weight or a rep every session (now {value}{unit})
goal.move.card_lift_stretch: add a little weight or a rep every session (now {value}{unit}, wished-for {stretch}{unit})
goal.move.card_lift_pending: add a little weight or a rep every session
goal.move.card_care: 5 min before & after · bracing on heavy lifts · body signals
goal.move.wrap_care: {axis} is carried every session instead of a number: 5 minutes of warm-up{sites}, 5 minutes of stretching after, and bracing breath before heavy lifts.
goal.move.wrap_transition: Next is the training program consult: training times, the split, and each session's exercises.
goal.move.phase_weeks_basis: Body change takes about 12 weeks to show clearly in the records
goal.move.pace_held_deficit: While cutting, I set {items} to hold steady.
goal.move.pace_held_surplus: While bulking, I set {items} to hold steady.
goal.move.direction_propose: Let’s align your training and nutrition with {name} for this phase.
goal.move.ask_baseline.approx:
I work out your daily calorie range from your weight.
If you do not know it exactly, about how many kg is it?
goal.move.direction_no_body: I am using your aim until the first body measurement; then I will recalculate.
goal.move.prac_two_allowed: You can do several together. Just say it, like "1 and 2".
goal.move.direction_no_baseline: There is no declared sex baseline, so I used your stated aim.
goal.move.ask_demographics.sex:
I need your sex to estimate your maintenance calories.
What is your sex?
goal.move.diet_nudge: Please share your first weight tomorrow morning so I can set the diet target.
goal.move.diet_statement: From maintenance {maint}, adjust by {change} to {kcal}. Protein uses {rate} per unit of {basis}.
goal.move.diet_changed: With the new record, daily target is about {kcal} and protein {protein}.
goal.move.direction_adjust_ask:
I redo your direction and pace around the timeframe and change you name.
What change do you want, and by when?
goal.move.ask_demographics.age:
I need your age to estimate your maintenance calories.
How old are you?
goal.move.direction_wish_basis: I adjusted the direction and pace for {wish}.
goal.move.diet_measure: A new body measurement will make this more accurate.
goal.move.diet_activity: Daily activity is based on {steps} strides.
goal.move.order_lead: Leaning out and building muscle pull against each other: building needs more food, leaning out needs less. Let's settle the order first.
goal.move.order_d_deficit: a leaner phase first, then eat more and build
goal.move.order_d_surplus: a building phase first, then eat less and lean out
goal.move.order_d_together: keep eating about the same and move both a little
goal.move.order_fact_high: Body fat is around {bf}% lately, above the {thr}% baseline.
goal.move.order_fact_low: Body fat is around {bf}% lately, below the {thr}% baseline.
goal.move.order_fact_high_trend: Body fat is around {bf}% lately, above the {thr}% baseline, and {trend}
goal.move.order_fact_low_trend: Body fat is around {bf}% lately, below the {thr}% baseline, and {trend}
goal.move.order_fact_high_1: Your body fat is {bf}% ({as_of}), above the {thr}% line.
goal.move.order_fact_low_1: Your body fat is {bf}% ({as_of}), below the {thr}% line.
goal.move.order_fact_high_1_trend: Your body fat is {bf}% ({as_of}), above the {thr}% line, and {trend}
goal.move.order_fact_low_1_trend: Your body fat is {bf}% ({as_of}), below the {thr}% line, and {trend}
goal.move.order_trend_up: your skeletal muscle is up {delta}kg on the readings before.
goal.move.order_trend_down: your skeletal muscle is down {delta}kg on the readings before.
goal.move.order_trend_flat: your skeletal muscle is about where it was.
goal.move.order_rec_deficit: I suggest option 1: keep the muscle you have and lean out first.
goal.move.direction_desc.cut: A cut means eating a little less to keep muscle while losing body fat. The opposite, eating more to build muscle, is called a bulk.
goal.move.direction_desc.recomp: A recomp keeps eating about the same while losing body fat and slowly adding muscle.
goal.move.direction_desc.lean_bulk: A lean bulk means eating a little more to build muscle while adding little body fat.
goal.move.direction_desc.bulk: A bulk means eating generously more to build muscle fast. Body fat rises with it.
goal.move.direction_amount.down: You would eat about {span}{unit} less a day.
goal.move.direction_amount.up: You would eat about {span}{unit} more a day.
goal.move.direction_amount_near: Almost the same: you would eat about {span}{unit} less a day.
goal.move.direction_amount_zero: You would eat about the same.
goal.move.direction_amount_none.down: There are no body numbers yet, so this can't be calculated. After your first InBody I will tell you how much less to eat a day.
goal.move.direction_amount_none.up: There are no body numbers yet, so this can't be calculated. After your first InBody I will tell you how much more to eat a day.
goal.move.direction_cap.down: {cap} is the limit. Cutting more than that loses muscle too.
goal.move.direction_cap.up: {cap} is the limit. Eating more than that adds more fat than muscle.
goal.move.direction_amount_then: The exact amount is set next, when you pick a pace.
goal.move.direction_food_snack_range: That is one snack to {hi} of rice.
goal.move.direction_food_range: That is about {lo} to {hi} of rice.
goal.move.direction_why_nobody: There are no body numbers yet, so I chose from your words "{aim}".
goal.move.direction_why_nobody_then: After your first InBody I will check the direction against the numbers again.
goal.move.direction_why_fat.high: Your body fat is around {bf}% lately. For {sex} above {thr}%, the body changes better by losing first and building after.
goal.move.direction_why_fat.low: Your body fat is around {bf}% lately. That is under the {thr}% line for {sex}, so now is a time to build rather than cut.
goal.move.direction_why_fat_1.high: Your body fat is {bf}% ({as_of}). For {sex} above {thr}%, the body changes better by losing first and building after.
goal.move.direction_why_fat_1.low: Your body fat is {bf}% ({as_of}). That is under the {thr}% line for {sex}, so now is a time to build rather than cut.
goal.move.direction_why_years.hold: After {years} of training your muscle is already built, so this phase keeps it rather than adding new.
goal.move.direction_why_years.hold_new: At {years} of training muscle still comes easily, so eating only a little less keeps it while the fat comes off.
goal.move.direction_why_years.grow_new: At {years} of training muscle still comes easily, so this phase builds it.
goal.move.direction_why_years.grow_exp: After {years} of training muscle comes slower than at first. Adding a little rather than a lot keeps the fat gain down.
goal.move.direction_why_years.recomp_exp: After {years} of training muscle comes slower than at first, so losing and building together shows slowly.
goal.move.direction_why_wish.mode: You said "{wish}", so I switched to {name}.
goal.move.direction_why_wish.faster: You said "{wish}", so I raised the pace.
goal.move.direction_why_wish.slower: You said "{wish}", so I slowed the pace.
goal.move.direction_why_wish.shorter: You said "{wish}", so I shortened the period and raised the pace.
goal.move.direction_why_wish.same: You said "{wish}"; your body numbers still point to {name}, so I kept the direction.
goal.move.direction_next.cut: Once body fat is down, the next phase builds volume.
goal.move.direction_next.recomp: Once body fat is down, the next phase focuses on building muscle.
goal.move.direction_next.lean_bulk: When body fat rises again, the next phase is a cut to tidy up.
goal.move.direction_next.bulk: When the bulk ends, the next phase is a cut to trim the added fat.
goal.move.pace_held_mode: While on the {mode}, I set {items} to hold steady.
goal.move.pace_p_fast.down: More fat comes off within {weeks} weeks
goal.move.pace_p_long: Same weekly change, over a longer stretch
goal.move.card_order_deficit_first: Cut first, build volume in the next phase
goal.move.card_order_surplus_first: Bulk first, cut in the next phase
goal.move.mode_chosen: We have chosen {name} for this phase.
goal.move.muscle_experienced: With your longer training history, recomp changes will be gradual.
goal.move.muscle_training_basis: This accounts for your training experience of {years}.
goal.move.recommend_changed: Your new body composition reading points toward {name}.
